messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Vyas <samir.vyas@orbitsys.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@orbitprocure.com>

Subject: MAP: evaluation milestones -> private-offer commit tranches (AWS)

Hi Samir / Priya,

Following our demo last week, attaching a draft MAP that ties evaluation milestones to staged private-offer commit tranches on AWS. High-level proposal:

- Week 0-4 (POC): no commit, 30-day eval credits (pilot access).
- Week 5-12 (Integration & Pilot): 6-month private-offer commitment tranche 1 = $75k — activates 10% list discount and 60% burst capacity.
- Month 4-9 (Ramp): tranche 2 = additional $150k commit to expand throughput (discount moves to 18%).
- Month 10 onward (Production): tranche 3 = annual commit $300k for sustained unit pricing and reserved capacity.

Each tranche unlocks: committed private-offer pricing on AWS Marketplace, reserved concurrency on Redwood Dedicated, and a one-time onboarding credit tied to the MAP milestone acceptance. We included clear acceptance criteria for each milestone in the attached MAP_Orbit_v2.pdf.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Orbit to confirm technical acceptance criteria for "Integration" milestone.
2) Procurement to confirm internal approval path for staggered tranches (POs/PO issuance cadence).
3) I'll loop in our Marketplace rep to confirm private-offer activation gating and DocuSign flow.

Goal: align timelines so private-offer activation for tranche 1 can be submitted to AWS by Dec 20 to meet Orbit's Jan pilot window.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min sync to walk through the MAP line-by-line.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0148

Thanks Laura — good outline. Two quick clarifications from procurement:

1) We need the tranche PO amounts to map to invoice milestones (not just calendar windows). Can you confirm the trigger event for tranche 2 ("Ramp")?
2) Is the 18% discount in tranche 2 applied to both hosted API and Marketplace-listed metering, or only reserved capacity SKUs? We need SKU-level clarity for our finance team.

Also copying our AWS marketplace contact to ensure the private-offer activation timeline is realistic: Jenna Park at AWS Marketplace (cc’d).

If you can send a condensed one-page commit schedule (PO triggers + DocuSign steps), we can route to legal tomorrow.

—Priya

Hi Priya — quick answers and an attached one-pager I prepared per your ask. See MAP commit-schedule table (also in attached MAP_Orbit_v2.pdf):

- Tranche 1 (Integration & Pilot) trigger: signed acceptance of pilot test cases (5 production-like integrations executed, defined latency threshold met for two core routes). Invoice: upon pilot acceptance (net30).
- Tranche 2 (Ramp) trigger: successful pilot + throughput test (sustained 5k QPS over a 24hr window on staging) OR 60 days of production traffic above mutually-agreed baseline. Invoice: split into two equal invoices at T+0 and T+90 days post-trigger.
- Tranche 3 (Production) trigger: formal production cutover + confirmed usage ramp to >=50% of committed throughput for 60 days. Annual invoice issued at activation, with monthly true-ups.

Discounts: the tranche discount % applies to Marketplace metered SKU pricing and Dedicated reserved SKU rates. Hosted API overage pricing follows the same unit rate table unless otherwise negotiated; we can carve out exceptions for specific SKUs if Orbit needs.

Attachments included: MAP_Orbit_v2.pdf (one-pager + acceptance criteria), and a condensed commit-schedule CSV stub.

I’ll coordinate directly with Jenna on the private-offer activation flow — typical AWS lead time for a new private-offer is 5–7 business days after DocuSign + PO, but that assumes payment terms and legal are finished.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Attachment: MAP_Orbit_v2.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB stub)

Subject: Re: MAP: evaluation milestones -> private-offer commit tranches (AWS)

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful. Legal pushed back on two items:

• Backloaded discounts: they want more protection if we delay tranche 2 (i.e., if Ramp doesn't hit timeline, can we retain a portion of tranche 1 discount retroactively?).
• SOW linkage: they want the MAP acceptance criteria cross-referenced in the SOW so invoicing is unambiguous. I attached a draft SOW excerpt for your team to confirm.

Attachment: Orbit_SOW_v1.docx (docx, 45KB stub)

Can Redwood confirm whether: (A) a partial-retention clause is possible (e.g., 6% baseline maintained if tranche 2 delays >60 days), and (B) whether we can append MAP acceptance checkboxes into the SOW so finance can auto-match POs to milestones.

I’ll wait for your confirmation before routing to our CFO.

—Samir
VP Product, Orbit Systems
samir.vyas@orbitsys.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: MAP: evaluation milestones -> private-offer commit tranches (AWS)

Samir — appreciate the details and the SOW excerpt. Quick replies: 

A) Partial-retention clause: yes — we can offer a fallback protection where a base discount (6%) survives if tranche 2 is delayed beyond 60 days, provided Orbit maintains the agreed minimal usage baseline. If delays extend beyond 120 days we revert to standard list pricing unless revised by mutual written amendment. We’ll include exact language in the DocuSign amendment.

B) SOW linkage: we can add MAP acceptance checkboxes into the SOW and include a simple invoice-matching table (milestone ID -> deliverable -> invoice trigger). That will help your AP team.

Next steps I will take today:
- Draft DocuSign amendment that includes the three tranches, partial-retention clause, and SOW linkage (will target to you by EOD PT).
- Loop Jenna to confirm AWS private-offer activation steps; Jenna, can you confirm 5–7 business-day lead time is still accurate for Orbit’s account?
- Marissa will follow up with finance to validate invoice schedule formatting.

If Orbit can sign tranche 1 amendment by Dec 17 we will submit to AWS and aim to have private-offer tokens active by Dec 24 — enough runway for your Jan pilot.

Thanks — happy to take a call if useful.

Laura Bennett
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
